title: Harborline Customer Accounts: Late-Issuance Goodwill Worked Through
content:
# Late-issuance goodwill worked through

> Harborline Customer Accounts

## 1. Subscription and lateness

The schedule reads the certificate subscription of the customer's most recent initial certificate issuance whenever that subscription is active and its initial certificate was issued more than 11 calendar days after the subscription's documents were complete; a certificate issued within that time is outside this schedule. The documents are complete on the subscription's organisation validation date for an OV or EV product (Harborline OV Single Domain, Harborline OV Wildcard, Harborline EV Single Domain, Harborline EV Multi-Domain) and on its order date for a DV product (Harborline DV Single Domain, Harborline DV Multi-Domain, Harborline DV Wildcard). Because the published issuance targets are at most five business days from complete documents and no such span, weekends and US federal holidays included, is longer than 11 calendar days, a certificate issued more than 11 calendar days after its documents were complete has always missed its target.

## 2. The figure

- The days the issuance was late are the calendar days from the documents-complete date to the date of the initial issuance, less 11.
- The subscription's daily value is its new-subscription charge divided by the calendar days from that charge's period start to its period end.
- The late-issuance goodwill figure is the subscription's daily value times the days the issuance was late.

## 3. From figure to grant

- For a grant under this schedule the yearly goodwill total is the sum of the goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today, a grant may not exceed the tier's per-case goodwill limit nor bring that yearly goodwill total above the tier's yearly goodwill limit, and a grant beyond either limit is made only up to the remaining limit; a goodwill grant made under none of Harborline's published service-failure goodwill schedules (late hosting provisioning, late recovery review decisions, same-day duplicate domain auto-renew charges, late certificate issuance, late recovery resets and late refund postings) remains under the base limit sentence.
- The late-issuance goodwill granted is the late-issuance goodwill figure limited in that way and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end; where the limited amount is zero, nothing is owed under this schedule and no entry is posted.
- In working the figure through to the amount granted, the figure is first multiplied by every multiplier that applies, the fixed uplifts that apply are then added, the limits are then applied, and only the final figure is rounded half up to the cent.

The per-case and yearly limits are the figures of the account's tier in the goodwill limits by tier.

## 4. Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A Harborline DV Single Domain subscription was ordered on 2 February and its initial certificate issued on 17 February: 15 days, so 4 days late. Its new-subscription charge of $47.45 covers a period of 365 calendar days, a daily value of $0.13. Figure: $0.13 times 4, $0.52. With room under both limits, $0.52 is granted.

Issued on 13 February instead (11 days): not more than 11, outside the schedule.
